title: No barriers to entry
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What stops other people from doing exactly what you do?

groups.heading: If I control the access, I control the content

lines.text: What kind of company would you buy, I asked, if you were the other chief executive, considering the times and the monopolies of the big three networks? A student said: a video streaming business. I said: way too soon. People are logging into dial-up. You had a modem and a little box. A student said: they want more distribution around the world.

Very good, I said. Somebody in distribution, giving people access to the internet. The assumption is: if I control the access, I'm going to control the content. If I control the cables going to people's homes, I control the television. That is how an internet access company comes into the picture.

That company was providing a service using the infrastructure of the telecoms, I said. It didn't own the phone line or the cable. It owned the software that gives you a signal, and it did the billing. It did not own a physical asset.

They misjudged it, I said. They thought this was a company that was really flying. The growth blinded them. But there were no barriers to entry for other people to get into that business. That was the biggest lesson.

Barriers to entry, I said, means there is something that stops others. A search company has one: its search algorithm. Nobody can come up with it. Here, there was no barrier. Everybody could become an internet service provider. I happened to be one of the first, in Panama. It's just a server. It became a commodity.

A company that is not turning a profit is buying a company that is profitable, in the billions, I said. And a company with decades in existence is getting bought by a company less than ten years old. You see how it was fertile ground for this catastrophic event to occur.

The lesson, I said: stick to the fundamentals. Never get blinded by the hype. Learn the fundamentals of your business, the net revenue. And the way you value a company is the net revenue times a multiple.
What is your barrier to entry?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write who else could do what you do.
Write what stops them: your barrier to entry.
Write what you own that is a real asset, not just a service.
Write whether your growth is real or just hype.
Write the fundamentals you will check: net revenue and a multiple.

check.q: What did I say was the biggest lesson about the access company?
choices: There were no barriers to entry

check.q: What did I say a barrier to entry means?
choices: Something that stops others from getting into the business

check.q: What did I say the lesson is?
choices: Stick to the fundamentals and don't get blinded by hype

recap: Know your barrier to entry. Don't be blinded by hype.
